candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review pertinent data before medication administration, monitor medication response/adverse effects, and provide safe medication care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — statin monitoring and hepatic safety
candidate.educational_objective: Know that atorvastatin labeling supports baseline consideration of liver-enzyme testing and repeat testing when clinically indicated rather than routine fixed monthly monitoring for every patient.

options.A: Obtain liver enzymes every month for every client taking atorvastatin regardless of symptoms or prior results.
options.B: Avoid all liver-enzyme testing after atorvastatin is started because transaminase results do not contribute to medication-safety assessment.
options.C: Wait to obtain any baseline liver assessment until symptoms of hepatic injury develop after therapy has already begun.
options.D: Consider liver-enzyme testing before atorvastatin is started and repeat testing when clinically indicated rather than on a fixed monthly schedule.

candidate.rationale: The current DailyMed LIPITOR label states: consider liver-enzyme testing before initiation and when clinically indicated thereafter. It does not require fixed monthly testing for all patients. Therefore D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current LIPITOR labeling advises considering liver-enzyme testing before initiation and repeating testing when clinically indicated, not on a universal fixed monthly schedule.
candidate.source_document_title: LIPITOR — atorvastatin calcium tablet, film coated
candidate.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Hepatic Dysfunction: consider liver enzyme testing before LIPITOR initiation and when clinically indicated thereafter; contraindicated in acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis.
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
candidate.stem: A client is starting atorvastatin. Which liver-enzyme monitoring plan is consistent with current labeling?
